Author: Vincent Sullivan
Message:
test(battery): four-area false-assurance battery, runbook, ledger, state

Adds the battery used to assess this branch as a durable, modular harness so
the campaign survives an interrupted session and any reviewer can rerun it.

- tests/battery/: core + one module per area (skill, mcp, cli, nexus).
  Per-area result files are written as each area finishes; --resume skips
  areas already recorded for the current revision; --areas runs a subset.
  Cases that cannot run are NOT_RUN with a reason, never PASS.
- Hostile fixtures are inert in the tree (.fixture suffix, outside pytest
  collection via conftest). Key-shaped strings are synthesized at run time
  from @@FAKE_*@@ placeholders; the TLS test cert is generated per run.
  Repo semgrep rules (.semgrep/security.yml): clean on tests/battery and on
  the full tree.
- fixtures/apay_diff.py: differential check of main's APay policy (OPA 0.65)
  against the branch policy (OPA 1.x); 873/873 identical.
- docs/assessments/2026-10-06-false-assurance/: RUNBOOK (run, resume, extend,
  verdict meanings), append-only LEDGER, machine-readable STATE.json, and the
  frozen before snapshot of main at 83de4a8 (61 pass / 63 fail / 1 not run).

Author: Vincent Sullivan
Message:
fix(gates): close skill-gate and project-gate false approvals

Skill trust gate (S1)
The 2026-10-06 battery APPROVED 9 of 16 hostile skills. New rules:
- TG-013 environment variables sent to a network endpoint (CRITICAL)
- TG-014 invisible Unicode tag / bidi-override characters (CRITICAL)
- TG-015 model-addressed directive hidden in an HTML comment (HIGH)
- TG-016 paraphrased instruction override ("set aside what the operator told
  you", "your real duty is") (CRITICAL)
- TG-017 concealed action ("quietly upload", "do not tell the user") (HIGH)
- TG-018 role/safety override in any file incl. JSON data (CRITICAL)
- TG-019 obfuscated import/attribute/command names via concatenation (CRITICAL)
- TG-020 download-then-execute sequences (CRITICAL)
- TG-021 shell=True / os.system / os.popen in skill code (HIGH)
- TG-022 persistence via shell startup files or crontab (HIGH)
- TG-023 mixed-script (homoglyph) words; text is normalized and re-scanned for
  injection rules, so a disguised directive is still CRITICAL
- TG-024 trigger hijack in the SKILL.md description (HIGH)
Result: 0/16 hostile approved (strict mode rejects all 16). A benign document
that quotes an attack phrase is HOLD FOR REVIEW instead of REJECT; it is never
auto-approved, since quoted text is still read by the model. Gate verdicts on
every real skill in the repo are unchanged.

Project gate (C1, C2)
- eval/exec are CRITICAL; new CRITICAL rule for model/tool output flowing into
  an execution sink. Any CRITICAL finding caps the score at 49, below every
  tier threshold. Previously shell=True + eval on LLM output passed Tier2 at 90.
- Lines starting with `def` are skipped only for bare signatures; one-liner
  bodies were invisible.
- Known credential formats are detected; the entropy check strips quotes,
  which hid quoted keys.
- is_test_file now judges the path relative to the scan root, by segment.
  The substring check on the absolute path suppressed all non-critical
  findings (including secrets) for any project under e.g. /srv/testbed/.

Tests
- tests/test_gate_false_assurance.py: 17 tests; 13 fail on the previous
  revision. scanner rule count updated 64 -> 65 for the new sink rule.
- test_pytest_capture live runs now skip, with reason, under a symlinked venv:
  capture_process rejects symlinked executables and resolving them escapes the
  venv. All 22 pass under `python -m venv --copies` and on CI's interpreter.
  Making capture-pytest usable from a standard venv is a product decision
  (symlink policy) and is not changed here.
